noise_floor_finding.headline: THE SWEEP IS NOISE-LIMITED, NOT SEARCH-LIMITED. The last 11 cycles of 'narrow the space' steering were re-ranking random draws. This is the single most important thing learned in the project so far and it re-frames every prior cycle.
noise_floor_finding.method: seed=1337 in ALL 467 metric-bearing runs, so every (config, lr) cell is n=1. But 5 config groups have >=4 full-rung runs that differ ONLY in lr, which gives a within-config replicate distribution to measure run-to-run spread directly.
noise_floor_finding.sigma_method: median MAD-sigma (1.4826 * median|x-median|) across the 5 within-config groups; each group n=4..41, medians 2.2686-2.3214, sds 0.0387-0.1137
noise_floor_finding.consequence_1_ranking_is_noise: The top-12 completed arms span 2.2378-2.2498 = 0.0120 BPC, which is 0.40 sigma. 134 of the 175 completed full-rung arms (77%) are within 1 sigma of the 'record'. Ranks 1-12 are a coin flip, not a ranking.
noise_floor_finding.consequence_2_winners_curse: The sweep ranks on min-of-N. Mean group MEAN is 2.3106 vs mean group MIN 2.2579, so the reported 'record' is overstated by ~0.0527 BPC on average purely by selection. Every 'new best' in this project's GPU history is partly luck.
noise_floor_finding.consequence_3_the_record_is_a_lucky_draw: Record 65dr5rv3 = 2.2378 sits 2.83 sigma BELOW the mean of its own config group (2.3224). It is not a superior config; it is a favourable draw from a noisy distribution.
noise_floor_finding.consequence_4_it_explains_stagnation: This is why 519 runs produced no movement: bayes was being fed a noisy objective, so it kept re-discovering the same configs and then 'improving' on them by luck. More search would NOT have helped. Replication had to come first.
noise_floor_finding.consequence_5_it_retroactively_softens_t: Last cycle's 'decoder inflation is empirically dead' still holds - ranks 2-12 are 1.6-2.2x the compute for +0.003..+0.012 BPC, and at 0.4 sigma that is now formally 'indistinguishable from free', which is an even STRONGER rejection of inflation. But the converse also holds: the record's 0.012 BPC lead over the cdl-10 arms is NOT evidence that cdl-6/tokFF-512 is a better architecture. Neither arm is distinguishable.
noise_floor_finding.revalidated_2026_09_29: Recomputed on the lr-matched CONVERGED subset (BPC<=2.5, lr in [0.00120,0.00140], n=60): robust within-config sigma = 0.0324 BPC, unchanged from last cycle's 0.0299 - the floor is real and stable. Winner's-curse inflation recomputes to 0.0528 BPC (mean group MEAN 2.3108 vs mean group MIN 2.2580). Top-12 converged arms span 0.0125 BPC = 0.39 sigma, so the ranking is still noise. The floor is NOT the reason the sweep is dead - see blocked_on.

kernel_clamp_finding.summary: The GPU sweep kernel does NOT enforce the anti-GPT-ification decoder caps, so every over-cap arm really trained over-cap. Proven from params/count, not inferred from the config echo.
kernel_clamp_finding.evidence: At fixed d_model=1024 / token_dec_layers=1 / token_emb_dim=128 / token_dec_nhead=8, params/count separates cleanly by requested token_dec_dim_ff: chunk_dec_layers=6 -> 10.18-10.34M at tokFF=512 vs 10.28-10.47M at tokFF=1024; chunk_dec_layers=4 -> 7.02-7.18M vs 7.15-7.31M. A working coerce_config clamp to 256 would have collapsed those pairs to identical counts.
kernel_clamp_finding.implication: The 0-cap-clean coverage gap is real, and the fold step must keep rejecting over-cap REQUESTED configs - a clamped-looking config echo is not evidence of a compliant model. The TPU kernel's coerce_config is the only place the caps bite.

seed_axis_defect.headline: LAST CYCLE'S 'FIX' WAS A DESIGN DEFECT. Adding seed=[1337,1338,1339] to fix replication made replication strictly IMPOSSIBLE, because bayes samples parameters independently and lr was continuous - the chance of two runs landing on the same (config, lr) cell is ~0.
seed_axis_defect.math: xqlix7jx had 9 free axes = 2592 discrete cells (with seed) x a CONTINUOUS lr. run_cap 160 => 0.062 runs per cell. Even with lr discrete it was 3*3*3*2*2*2*2*2*3 = 1728 cells => 0.093 runs/cell. You cannot replicate a cell you visit 0.06 times.
seed_axis_defect.measured_proof: Across 362 full-rung bs32 arms, only 5 distinct config-groups reached n>=3, and the largest (cdl10/tff1024) had 27 converged runs that differ ONLY in lr - a replicate set the sweep produced by ACCIDENT via continuous lr, not by design. The seed axis tripled the space and bought zero guaranteed replicates.
seed_axis_defect.correction: Make EVERY free axis discrete so the space is enumerable at 54 cells, then let run_cap 200 deliver 3.7 runs/cell. Replication is then a structural property of the design, not a hope.

divergence_finding.headline: 62% OF ALL GPU ARMS DIVERGED AND THE PRIOR 13 CYCLES NEVER NOTICED, because they ranked on min-BPC, which hides a collapsed majority behind one lucky tail.
divergence_finding.measurement: Among 334 finished full-rung bs32 arms, only 127 (38.0%) converge to BPC<=2.5; 207 (62.0%) sit at BPC 2.5-6.8. Train CE separates them cleanly: converged ~1.33-1.67, diverged ~2.05-2.58.
divergence_finding.cause_is_lr: Divergence rate by lr bin: 90.9% below 0.00080, 87.7% in [0.0008,0.0010), 64.2% in [0.0010,0.00115), 28.6% in [0.00115,0.00125), then 0-25% above 0.00125. The lr range that bayes spent most of its budget in was the range where the model mostly explodes.
divergence_finding.why_it_matters: Two reasons. (1) The 'noise floor' sigma=0.0324 BPC was measured over converged arms, but the ARMS THAT POPULATE THE TAIL are 62% of the record - so min-of-N over all arms is dominated by a heavy right tail, which is precisely the selection bias that manufactured the 2.2378 'record'. (2) Any future sweep must either raise the lr floor or accept that 2 of every 3 runs are dead weight.
divergence_finding.cost_is_cheap: Divergence is NOT a compute leak: diverged arms cost 76.5 GPU-h total vs 422.0 GPU-h converged (15.3% of GPU time), median runtime 600s vs 12526s. They die early. So this is a MEASUREMENT problem, not a budget problem - consistent with the anti-inflation rule.

unprobed_axis_finding.headline: ch - THE CORE PerPos COMPRESSION-RATIO KNOB - HAS ZERO COVERAGE IN 519 RUNS. The sweep has spent its entire life on decoder/regularizer plumbing and never once tested the one hyperparameter that defines the novel architecture.
unprobed_axis_finding.evidence: All 519 runs (and all 362 full-rung bs32 arms) used ch=4. ch=2 and ch=3 have never been trained. chunk size is what sets the compression ratio of ChunkCompressorEmbedding and hence the length of the chunk-level AR sequence - it is the single most PerPos-specific knob in the config.
unprobed_axis_finding.second_gap: chunk_use_alibi has never been varied either (all 519 = False), despite the TPU side listing ALiBi evaluation as an open direction in baseline.json.
unprobed_axis_finding.correction: ch [2,3,4] is now free in 8p4t1juu - the first time this axis is ever trained.

operating_point_mismatch.headline: The GPU sweep is not measuring at the committed budget, and never has. This is a legitimate measurement choice, but it means GPU-sweep BPC is not directly comparable to the TPU-side fold bar.
operating_point_mismatch.committed_budget_vs_sweep: baseline.json committed_budget: limit_chars=10M, block_size=512, batch_size=384. The GPU sweep kernel pins batch_size=32, block_size=256, limit_chars=10M. Batch is 1/12 and block is 1/2 of the committed point; with ~2x the epochs and ~2x the samples per step the sweep is a legitimately different operating point.
operating_point_mismatch.why_it_is_not_inflation: Smaller batch + smaller block is LESS compute per step, not more. The sweep's rejected arms all confirm this: bs 48/64/96 (MORE batch) were uniformly worse (best 2.3995 / 2.6503 / 3.7496), because larger batch at this lr diverges. So the pinned small batch is not a way to buy BPC - it is a hard constraint.
operating_point_mismatch.the_consequence: TPU best under committed budget = 1.86000 BPC in 1169s (s1y9s6hj). GPU sweep record = 2.23781 BPC in 10666s. The GPU sweep is 0.378 BPC WORSE and 9.1x SLOWER. Cross-side BPC gaps of this size are confounded by the operating point, so GPU arms can only be folded on CONFIG evidence, not by matching the TPU number. This is the formal reason fold_target requires cap-clean + budget-matched, and why 0 arms qualify.
operating_point_mismatch.do_not: Do not 'fix' this by raising batch_size/block_size in the sweep - that would be compute inflation, the exact cheat the caps exist to prevent.
